name: Geoff's Woodworking
old_description: With over 40 years of experience, Geoff's Woodworking has earned the reputation as a respected and dedicated high-end woodworking business. We produce a wide range of beautiful custom work with personal attention to detail and quality. Our specialties range from magnificent entry doors to kitchen cabinets, custom furniture, finishing and refinishing, antique reproduction, historical restoration and conservation. From design to construction to finishing and installation, we thrive on finding creative, elegant ways to realize your vision. If you are looking for something beyond run-of-mill factory furniture and prefab cabinets, you've found the right place.
about:
Geoff's Woodworking was founded in 1986 in Richmond, California, by Geoff Arko. The shop operates as a high-end custom woodworking business serving the San Francisco Bay Area. With over four decades of experience, the business has built a reputation for personal attention to detail and quality.

The company produces custom furniture, kitchen cabinets, and entry doors, and provides finishing, refinishing, antique reproduction, historical restoration, and conservation services. It handles projects from design through construction, finishing, and installation, functioning as a full-service architectural millwork shop. The workshop focuses on custom work rather than mass-produced items.

Clients include homeowners, interior designers, architects, and contractors seeking custom residential and commercial millwork. The shop has worked on historical preservation projects and creates antique reproductions alongside contemporary custom pieces. Its specialties range from magnificent entry doors to kitchen cabinets and custom furniture.

Geoff's Woodworking distinguishes itself by offering a complete design-to-installation process and by focusing on creative, elegant solutions that go beyond factory-produced furniture and prefabricated cabinets. The company thrives on finding creative, elegant ways to realize client visions.
